1. Purpose
This manual defines the preventive maintenance (PM) activities, operating parameters and common alarms
for the TX-200 CNC turning centres (machines CNC-04 to CNC-09) used on the shaft machining line.
2. Safety First
Before starting any maintenance activity other than daily operator checks, the machine must be isolated as
per SAF-SOP-003 Lockout/Tagout. Never open the electrical cabinet or hydraulic circuit on a running or
energised machine.

7. Replacing a Hydraulic Hose
 1.  Isolate the machine as per SAF-SOP-003, including releasing stored hydraulic pressure.
 2.  Confirm the panel pressure gauge reads zero before loosening any fitting.
 3.  Place a drip tray under the hose and loosen the fittings slowly.
 4.  Fit a new hose of the same rating and tighten fittings.
 5.  Remove locks as per SAF-SOP-003, start the hydraulic unit and confirm pressure returns to 3.5 - 4.0
 MPa with no leaks.

1. Purpose
This procedure describes how incoming raw materials and bought-out components are inspected at the
receiving area before they are released to stores and production.
2. Scope
Applies to all steel bar stock, castings, forgings and bought-out components received at the Hosur plant.
3. Responsibilities
   Stores Executive: receives material, checks quantity against the delivery challan and informs QC.
   QC Inspector: carries out sampling, visual and dimensional inspection, and records results.
   QC Supervisor: approves acceptance or rejection of the lot.

4. Procedure
 1.  Stores Executive places the received lot in the Incoming Inspection Area and raises an inspection
 request.
2.  QC Inspector collects the purchase order, drawing and supplier test certificate (if available).
 3.  Draw 5 samples at random from every lot, irrespective of lot size.
 4.  Perform visual inspection for rust, dents, cracks and burrs.
 5.  Perform dimensional inspection on all critical dimensions using a vernier caliper.
 6.  If all 5 samples are within specification, the lot is accepted. If any sample fails, the complete lot is
 rejected.
7.  Record results on paper form QF-07 Incoming Inspection Report and file it in the QC office.
 8.  Accepted material is tagged with a GREEN tag and moved to stores.
 9.  Rejected material is tagged with a RED tag and kept in the Red Bin area near Gate 2 until it is returned
 to the supplier.
10.  QC Supervisor informs Purchase by email about rejected lots by end of the shift.
 
5. Records
   QF-07 Incoming Inspection Report (paper) - retained for 2 years.

2. Scope

4. Sampling Plan
Defects are classified as follows:
   Critical: a defect that can cause a safety risk or failure of the part, e.g. crack, wrong material grade, or a
 dimension out of tolerance on a characteristic marked Critical.
  Major: a defect that affects fit or function but is not critical, e.g. deep dent, damaged thread, or a
 dimension out of tolerance on a characteristic marked Major.
  Minor: a cosmetic defect that does not affect fit or function, e.g. light surface marks or light surface rust
 that can be removed by cleaning.

1. Purpose
To protect people from the unexpected start-up of machines or release of stored energy (electrical, hydraulic,
pneumatic, mechanical) during maintenance, cleaning, setting or repair.
2. Scope
Applies to all employees and contract workers at the Hosur plant who maintain, clean or repair machines,
including CNC turning centres, presses and compressors.
3. Definitions
   Authorised person: a trained employee who applies their own personal lock and tag to isolate energy.
   Affected person: an operator or employee who works in the area but does not perform the isolation.
   Zero energy state: the condition where all energy sources are isolated and stored energy is released, so
 that the machine cannot move or release energy.
4

rform the isolation.
   Zero energy state: the condition where all energy sources are isolated and stored energy is released, so
 that the machine cannot move or release energy.
4. Lockout Procedure
 1.  Inform all affected persons that the machine is being shut down for maintenance.
 2.  Stop the machine using the normal stop sequence.
 3.  Isolate all energy sources: main electrical isolator, compressed air valve, and hydraulic power unit.
 4.  Apply your personal red lock and danger tag to each isolation point. Each authorised person working
 on the machine applies their own lock. Use a multi-lock hasp when more than one person is involved.
5.  Release stored energy: bleed hydraulic pressure and accumulators until the gauge reads zero, vent
 compressed air to 0 bar, and block any parts that can fall under gravity.
6.  Verify zero energy: try to start the machine from the control panel and confirm it does not start. Confirm
 all pressure gauges read zero. Return controls to OFF.
5. Removing Locks
 1.  Check that tools and materials are removed and guards are refitted.

 all pressure gauges read zero. Return controls to OFF.
5. Removing Locks
 1.  Check that tools and materials are removed and guards are refitted.
 2.  Confirm all persons are clear of the machine.
 3.  Each authorised person removes only their own lock. Nobody may remove another person's lock.
 4.  Inform affected persons that the machine is being restarted.
 
6. Removal of a Lock When the Owner Is Absent
If an authorised person has left the plant without removing their lock, the lock may be removed only through
this procedure:
 1.  The Shift Supervisor makes every reasonable effort to contact the lock owner by phone.
 2.  If the owner cannot be reached, the Production Manager and the Safety Officer must both authorise
 removal.
3.  The machine is physically inspected to confirm it is safe to re-energise.
